title: Introduce row-stability anchors and density-animation guidelines for virtualized tables
creator: Samantha Chu
description:
Problem: Virtualized tables in the design system currently produce visual jank and contextual loss when rows shift due to sorting, filtering, or batch updates. This is especially noticeable in high-density modes where multiple rows are inserted/removed and during column-resize interactions. Users report losing their focus row (the row they are interacting with) when the list reflows, causing repeated clicks/scrolls and poor perceived stability.

Goal: Define a set of design patterns, token updates, and motion guidelines that engineers and designers can implement to preserve perceived row position (row-stability anchors), smooth density transitions, and minimal-motion fallbacks for accessibility. Deliverables should include spec language, component-level CSS/animation recommendations, density transition token proposals, and an implementation checklist for engineering.

Key constraints:
- Must work with virtualized rendering (windowing) where only a subset of rows are in DOM.
- Interactions to cover: sort, filter, bulk mutate (multi-row updates), column resize, keyboard re-order focus, and paged loading.
- Performance budget: animation must not add >15ms main-thread overhead per frame in typical workloads on mid-range laptop hardware.
- Respect prefers-reduced-motion and low-power mode.
- Maintain SR (screen reader) announcement parity; do not duplicate announcements on animation start/end.
design_decision_record: We will introduce a row anchor system: the table will pick a stable anchor row (focus row or top visible row) and try to maintain its visual position by adjusting the virtualization offset during reflow. Animations will be purely transform-based (translateY) where possible to avoid layout thrash. Density changes will animate opacity + transform with short durations and cubic-bezier easing tuned for perception. For large diffs (>8 row changes visible) we will fall back to an instant crossfade to avoid long-running animations and heavy reflow. prefers-reduced-motion collapses transitions to immediate state changes. Use of GPU-accelerated transform and will avoid expensive box-shadow and large repaint-causing properties during animations.
acceptance_criteria: Anchor logic: When a user has row focus (mouse or keyboard), sorting/filtering keeps that focused row visually near its pre-change vertical position unless user scrolls intentionally.
Density transitions: switching between density modes animates only position and opacity; no layout jank on mid-range hardware under typical table sizes (~200 visible rows).
Performance: End-to-end animation frame time increase <= 15ms on test harness (Mid-2020 MacBook Pro equivalent) for a 6-row visible change scenario.
Accessibility: prefers-reduced-motion collapses animations; screen reader announces change once. Keyboard navigation remains contiguous and focusable during transitions.
Engineering: Implementation contains a small public API to opt-in/out of anchors, and docs include telemetry events to measure anchor success rate and jank occurrences.
notes_and_tradeoffs:
Trade-offs considered: 1) Trying to preserve pixel-perfect positions for all rows is expensive and brittle with virtualization; we limit to preserving either the focused row or top anchor row to reduce complexity. 2) Using transforms avoids reflow but means certain layout-dependent decorations (e.g., zebra striping that depends on DOM order) may require additional CSS parity handling. 3) We will not attempt to animate column-resize re-layouts beyond individual cell translate; full table relayout animations are out of scope for this ticket. 4) Telemetry will add lightweight counters only; heavy tracing is deferred to a follow-up.

Open questions: How to present token-level density timelines in the design token catalog? (We propose density.motion.duration-short/duration-medium and easing.density-in/out tokens.)
implementation_guidance:
- Anchor selection: priority = focusedRowId > hoveredRowId > topVisibleRow. Compute desired translate delta and apply transform to row container.
- Virtualization offset compensation: when anchor moves out of virtual window due to insert/remove above, adjust window start index by delta to keep anchor in viewport.
- Use will-change: transform and avoid animating height/width. For opacity+translate, prefer composite-only properties.
- Fallback plan: if the virtualization library cannot compensate reliably, enable cross-fade on the table body with aria-live polite announcement of 'rows updated'.
- Token proposals: density.motion.duration-short = 100ms, density.motion.duration-medium = 180ms, density.motion.easing = cubic-bezier(0.2,0.9,0.3,1). Provide examples in the token catalog.
- QA checklist: verify 3 densities (compact, default, spacious), sort/filter/bulk-update scenarios, keyboard-only navigation, screen reader validation, turn on/off prefers-reduced-motion.
comments: 2025-02-10 Samantha Chu: Ticket created after user research session where 7/12 participants lost context after rapid sort changes. Initial spike recommends anchor approach.
2025-02-12 Aisha Patel: Ran prototype in Storybook; observed acceptable smoothness for single-row moves. Need to tighten durations for compact mode.

2025-02-14 Leo Martinez (eng): Reviewed anchoring approach; raised concern about virtualization library edge-case where anchor is removed from DOM mid-animation. Suggested adding cancel-safe fallback and telemetry.
2025-02-16 Design critique: Reduced-motion behavior validated. Minor UI tweak: add 1px focus halo during transforms to improve discoverability when row translates.
2025-02-18 Aisha Patel: Implemented token suggestions in token branch. Open PR referenced. Perf harness shows 12ms additional main-thread time in 6-row diff test (within budget).
2025-02-20 Samantha Chu: Updated acceptance criteria to include telemetry event names and performance budget. Preparing handoff doc for eng and QA.
next_steps: 1) Finalize token names and add to token catalog (Aisha). 2) Engineering spike to add offset compensation API in virtualization layer (Leo). 3) QA: Create test harness scenarios and perf run. 4) Ship as opt-in table prop for console-2025.03 and enable by default in console-2025.04 after telemetry validation.
telemetry_proposal: Events: table.anchor.apply (success|fallback), table.motion.jank (ms), table.density.switch (from->to, duration). Track counts and 95th percentile jank per route.
